claims.claim: Morgan Stanley reported second-quarter 2026 net revenues of $21.3 billion.
Second-quarter 2026 diluted EPS was $3.46.
Second-quarter 2026 ROTCE, a non-GAAP measure, was 26.6%.
Record results were led by Equity.
Wealth Management net new assets of $148 billion were a record.
Net revenues were $21,348 million versus $16,792 million a year ago.
Pre-tax income was $7,348 million versus $4,622 million a year ago.
The release describes firm net revenues and pre-tax income as records.
The record designation is footnoted as records for a reported quarterly period excluding DVA and reflecting the current reporting structure.
Net income applicable to Morgan Stanley was $5,581 million, or $3.46 per diluted share.
A year ago net income applicable to Morgan Stanley was $3,539 million, or $2.13 per diluted share.
Return on equity was 20.7% versus 13.9% a year ago.
Return on tangible common equity was 26.6% (non-GAAP) versus 18.2% a year ago.
Compensation expense was $8,187 million and non-compensation expenses were $5,715 million.
The expense efficiency ratio was 65% versus 71% a year ago.
The release highlights the same 65% expense efficiency ratio for the first half of the year.
Provision for credit losses was $98 million versus $196 million a year ago.
The effective tax rate was 23.1% versus 22.7% a year ago.
Institutional Securities net revenues were $11,040 million versus $7,643 million a year ago.
The release describes Institutional Securities net revenues as a record.
Institutional Securities pre-tax income was $4.3 billion versus $2.1 billion a year ago.
Institutional Securities Investment Banking net revenues were $2,437 million, up 58%.
Equity net revenues were $6,300 million, up 69%, with notable strength in Asia.
Fixed Income net revenues were $2,455 million, up 13%.
Institutional Securities Other net revenues were negative $152 million versus positive $202 million a year ago.
The decline in Other net revenues was driven by higher mark-to-market losses on corporate loans, inclusive of hedges.
Wealth Management net revenues were $8,856 million, up 14%.
Wealth Management pre-tax income was $2.7 billion and pre-tax margin was 30.5%.
Wealth Management net new assets were $148.1 billion versus $59.2 billion a year ago.
The release states just over half of net new assets represented inflows related to IPOs of certain Workplace-channel clients.
Wealth Management fee-based client assets were $3,022 billion.
Wealth Management loans were $195.7 billion.
Investment Management net revenues were $1,646 million, up 6%.
Investment Management pre-tax income was $404 million versus $323 million a year ago.
Investment Management AUM was $2,004 billion.
Investment Management long-term net flows were $7.5 billion versus $12.2 billion a year ago.
The release provides no guidance, outlook or financial targets for any future period.
Standardized CET1 was 14.8%, versus 15.0% a year ago.
Advanced CET1 was 16.2%.
Tier 1 leverage was 6.0% and SLR was 4.9%, versus 6.8% and 5.5% a year ago.
Capital ratios are stated as estimates subject to change in the Form 10-Q.
Book value per share was $67.80.
Tangible book value per share was $53.18 (non-GAAP).
The Firm repurchased $1,500 million of stock during the quarter at an average price of $197.64.
The Board reauthorized a share repurchase program of up to $20 billion beginning in 3Q26.
The Board declared a $1.15 quarterly dividend, an increase of 15 cents.
Wealth Management net new assets more than doubled year over year.
Fee-based asset flows fell to $39.1 billion from $42.8 billion.
The provision for credit losses reflects portfolio growth plus individual assessments for certain corporate and commercial real estate loans.
Standardized CET1, Tier 1 leverage and SLR all stand below year-ago levels.
